findings.claim: CompositeResolverTemplate emits ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally, ignoring the new Options.Generator.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage and the documented opt-out. README says opt-out via GeneratedMessagePackResolver(ExcludeFromCodeCoverage=false), but composite resolvers cannot be opted out, and the test for opt-out does not cover composite resolvers.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a CompositeResolver with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage=false and assert the output has no [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]; it will fail because the template has no condition.

findings.claim: The change adds a public opt-out property, GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, plus PublicAPI entries, though the requirement says no setting is needed. The API is optional per the requirement but permanent public surface; it is not recorded as a team preference.

receipt_plan.detail: REQ-2297: 'I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too'; the new public property and 4 PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt entries are added with no maintainer sign-off.

findings.claim: The attribute is skipped on netstandard2.0/.NETFRAMEWORK, so 'all generated code' is not covered on those targets. The README documents this limitation. Coverage is still skewed for those consumers.

receipt_plan.detail: Guard '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK' in every template; README line 1640 documents the limitation.

questions.text: Should the opt-out setting exist, or should the attribute be unconditional?
options: Keep the opt-out property (ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on GeneratedMessagePackResolver)
Remove the setting and always emit the attribute
questions.why_it_matters: If unconditional is preferred, the new public API, options plumbing and template conditions are unnecessary scope. If the opt-out is kept, the composite resolver template must honor it.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Emit the attribute on all generated formatters and resolvers by default, with an opt-out property GeneratedMessagePackResolver.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage (default true), guarded by #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Emit the attribute unconditionally in every template with no setting. Remove the attribute property, the GeneratorOptions flag, the AnalyzerUtilities parsing and the PublicAPI entries, and drop the opt-out test and README sentence.
